channel.title: Bloomberg — diagnostic source feed
channel.description: Diagnostic feed grouped by acquisition connector.

item.title: The Key Takeaways From Micron's Better-Than-Expected Forecast
item.description: Hendi Susanto, a research analyst and portfolio manager at Gabelli, reacts to Micron Technology giving a sales forecast for the current quarter that shattered estimates after the AI building frenzy fueled unprecedented demand. He speaks on "Bloomberg The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Micron Forecast Tops Estimates on Booming AI Memory Demand
item.description: Micron Technology Inc., the largest US maker of memory chips, gave a sales forecast for the current quarter that shattered estimates after the AI building frenzy fueled unprecedented demand. Revenue will be about $61.5 billion in the fiscal first quarter, which runs through November, the company said in a statement Wednesday. Analysts estimated $56.8 billion on average. Excluding some items, profit will be about $38.15 a share, compared with a projection of $36.02. We get reaction from Jake Silverman, Bloomberg Intelligence Semiconductor Analyst. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Former NY Governor Cuomo Buys $9.6 Million Hamptons Estate
item.description: Former New York Governor Andrew Cuomo purchased a roughly seven-acre estate on the south shore of Long Island for $9.6 million, according to a spokesperson and property records.
item.dc:creator: Cameron Fozi and Laura Nahmias

item.title: Kalshi Finalizing New Funding at $40 Billion Value Ahead of IPO
item.description: Kalshi Inc. is finalizing a new financing round that would value the prediction market platform at around $40 billion, according to people familiar with the matter. The deal is expected to be the startup’s last round before an initial public offering, which is anticipated as soon as next year, the people said.
item.dc:creator: Natasha Mascarenhas and Denitsa Tsekova

item.title: Ackman on AI & IPOs, Climate Costs, Paramount's Debt Raise
item.description: A weekly, midday program that delivers high-impact, editorially driven coverage of the most important corporate transactions shaping the global market. Today's guests: Pershing Square CEO & Founder Bill Ackman, Pulse Fund Founder & Managing Partner Tenzin Seldon, EQT Partner, Head of AI Infrastructure Jan Vesely, BCG Global Head of Sustainable Investing Vinay Shandal, and JPMorgan Private Bank Global Head of Alternative Investments Kristin Kallergis Rowland. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Micron Forecast Tops Estimates on Booming Demand for Memory
item.description: Micron Technology Inc., the largest US maker of memory chips, gave a sales forecast for the current quarter that shattered estimates after the AI building frenzy fueled unprecedented demand.
item.dc:creator: Dina Bass

item.title: Amazon Nuke Deal to Help Expand Constellation Maryland Site
item.description: Amazon.com Inc. has agreed to purchase 690 megawatts of power from Constellation Energy Corp. in a deal that will help the biggest US nuclear operator boost capacity at the only reactors in Maryland.
item.dc:creator: Will Wade

item.title: Google Grapples With Employee Skepticism About New Gemini 4
item.description: Alphabet Inc.’s Google has begun rolling out Gemini 4 Argon, its long-awaited flagship artificial intelligence model, but the company is grappling with internal skepticism over how well it performs in key areas, such as coding.
item.dc:creator: Julia Love and Davey Alba

item.title: Robinhood CEO Says New AI-Driven Agent Apps Are Safe
item.description: Robinhood Markets Chairman and CEO Vlad Tenev discusses the firm’s new AI-driven agent apps unveiled during a Houston summit. Speaking on "Bloomberg The Close," Tenev outlines a vision of giving individual traders hedge fund-like tools, including 24/7 trading across asset classes, autonomous “agent loops” that can operate while users sleep, and access to specialized data sources such as satellite imagery and blockchain analytics. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Biggest US Grid Suspends Plan for Data Center Power Auction
item.description: The operator of the biggest US electric grid suspended plans for an auction it had planned to help meet surging electric demand from data centers.
item.dc:creator: Brian Eckhouse and Naureen S. Malik

item.title: Embedding AI Risks Into Investments: Rowland
item.description: Kristin Kallergis Rowland, global head of alternative investments at JPMorgan Private Bank, joins Dani Burger on "Bloomberg Deals." Kristin Kallergis Rowland explains how an investor ends up being on both the bull and bear side of AI. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Flow Engineering Raises $50M to Bring AI to Hardware
item.description: As AI is moving beyond software and deeper into the physical world, Flow Engineering just raised $50 million at a $750 million valuation to help companies use AI agents to design and build hardware. Flow Engineering founder and CEO Pari Singh and Roelof Botha, Flow investor and board member - formerly at Sequoia Capital - join Ed Ludlow to discuss how faster hardware development could support a broader revival of US manufacturing. They speak on "Bloomberg Tech." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: OpenAI’s $30B Bet, Trump’s AI Safety Shift and Apple’s Next Act
item.description: Bloomberg’s Ed Ludlow breaks down OpenAI's plan to raise at least $30 billion from investors in a new round of funding after pushing back its plans for an IPO. Plus, President Trump supports using outside auditors to assess the safety of AI systems after meeting with Silicon Valley leaders; and Apple keeps pushing the envelope under new CEO John Ternus with plans to make its foray into the smart-home market. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Saronic CEO: 'Speed Is Everything' in Shipbuilding
item.description: Saronic is breaking ground on what it says will be the largest and most advanced shipyard in America. Saronic co-founder and CEO Dino Mavrookas joins Ed Ludlow to discuss how its Port Alpha in Brownsville, Texas, is at the center of the defense tech company's push to rapidly scale production of autonomous ships. He speaks on "Bloomberg Tech." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: MercadoLibre’s Brazil Drug Marketplace Faces Regulator Review
item.description: MercadoLibre Inc.’s push to expand its sale of prescription drugs in Brazil is facing a setback after the nation’s health regulator said it’s reviewing the e-commerce company’s plan to create an online marketplace for pharmacies.
item.dc:creator: Rachel Gamarski and Felipe Saturnino

item.title: OpenAI Blames Moonshot for Mass Data Extraction on Its AI Models
item.description: OpenAI accused its Chinese rival Moonshot AI of being responsible for a wide-scale effort to extract data from its GPT artificial intelligence systems that could be used to reproduce the reasoning and capabilities of the company’s most advanced models.
item.dc:creator: Maggie Eastland

item.title: AI Infrastructure Firm Accelevation Edges Down 0.3% Post-IPO
item.description: Shares of Accelevation Holdings Corp., a data center infrastructure company, declined 0.3% after the company and its private equity backer raised $540 million in an initial public offering priced below its marketed range.
item.dc:creator: Matthew Griffin

item.title: Bitcoin Rides Risk Roller Coaster as Speculative Bets Wind Down
item.description: Bitcoin enjoyed a brief respite along with other risk assets such as stocks amid the expectation that another rate hike is unlikely next month.
item.dc:creator: David Pan

item.title: AI Cycles Are Running in Tandem, Says JPMorgan's Sundar
item.description: Sitara Sundar, head of alternative investment strategy at JPMorgan Private Bank, says diversifying across the AI value chain is the best strategy for investors. Sundar also says volatility we see now in the tech space is healthy. She speaks to Bloomberg's Dani Burger on "Open Interest." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Micron’s $370 Billion Stock Rebound Hinges on AI Spending View
item.description: Micron Technology Inc. shares have rebounded from a summer selloff as fears about a potential pullback in AI spending have faded. Now investors want assurances from the memory-chip maker that the long-term outlook for demand remains bright.
item.dc:creator: Carmen Reinicke
